findings:
🟠 [py-shim-sigpipe-ign] MUST-FIX hooks/tests/run.sh outer child shim: CPython sets SIGPIPE and SIGXFSZ to SIG_IGN at startup, and `os.execvp` does not restore them (only `subprocess` does, via restore_signals). The shim resets only INT/TERM/QUIT, so the inner run.sh and every suite under it inherit SIGPIPE ignored, which bash cannot reset or trap. Impact: only in snapshot mode with python3 present, pipeline writers get EPIPE instead of SIGPIPE (`yes | head -1` prints "Broken pipe" and exits 1 instead of a silent 141), a divergence G4 does not name that can turn stderr-exact or pipefail-sensitive suites red in the both-modes comparison. Smallest fix: add `signal.SIGPIPE` and `signal.SIGXFSZ` to the tuple reset to SIG_DFL before `os.execvp`; minimum shippable version is this diff plus that one-line change.
🔵 [pgid-int-trap-indistinct] CUT/FOLLOW-UP The process-group case asserts outer exit 130, which is also what an untrapped default SIGINT death of the inner would give. It still catches the original defect (same group, SIGINT ignored) through the PGID assertions and the 30s sleep, so a trap-specific marker is optional hardening.
🔵 [relwrite-fail-continues] CUT/FOLLOW-UP If `fail` in lib.sh (not in the diff) records and continues, the relative-write case still proceeds after a failed build. The `cd "$snap/repo" || exit 1` subshell guard stops the write landing in the runner's cwd, so the Finding 1 hazard is closed; an early exit from the case is cosmetic.
🔵 [outer-shutdown-group-wait] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `__ts_outer_on_interrupt` forwards the signal to the child group and waits on the child pid only, not G5's "TERM the group and wait until the group is gone", and its traps are installed after the child starts. The signal exit-path cases (INT with a delayed descendant, TERM mid-construction, reaper) are outside this pass's four findings and required tests.
